title: Time-varying effects of revascularisation versus medical therapy on spontaneous MI and cardiac death in stable coronary disease: reconstructed-IPD network meta-analysis

pico.population: Adults with chronic coronary syndrome, stratified by presentation, ischaemia burden, anatomy and LV function
pico.intervention: Routine revascularisation (PCI or CABG) plus medical therapy, including FFR-guided PCI
pico.comparator: Initial medical therapy alone, or sham/placebo PCI where available
pico.outcomes: Cardiac death, spontaneous MI, all-cause death, with time-varying hazard ratios and restricted mean survival time
pico.timing: Follow-up from randomisation to the longest reported, 1 to 15 years

decision: Whether and when to offer revascularisation for prognosis, not only symptoms, in stable coronary disease, and how to counsel on early procedural hazard against later spontaneous-MI benefit.
decision_maker: Interventional cardiologists, heart teams and guideline committees
why_now: Two meta-analyses reached different conclusions on cardiac death (PMIDs 32794407, 34002203), and trials since, including extended ISCHEMIA follow-up (36335918), long-term FAME follow-up (41540107), REVIVED (36027563) and the ISCHEMIA CTO analysis (40139890), report non-proportional effects that trial-level relative risks cannot capture.

competing.note: ISCHEMIA-CTO: CTO subpopulation only, MACE at 5 years
PCI-GULF: ischaemic cardiomyopathy with reduced LVEF only
RESTORE-PCI: ischaemic LV dysfunction only

designs.primary: Reconstructed individual patient data network meta-analysis from published Kaplan-Meier curves, with flexible parametric or RMST models and prespecified effect modification by ischaemia, anatomy and LV function
designs.alternative: One-stage IPD meta-analysis if ISCHEMIA, FAME 2 and REVIVED investigators share data

data_required: Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk for cardiac death, spontaneous MI and all-cause death from the randomised revascularisation versus medical therapy trials, with MI definitions per trial
data_sources: Trial investigators for IPD where available
feasibility: High for the reconstructed-IPD analysis, which is the owner's established method; MI definition heterogeneity across eras is the main technical risk. IPD route would need a consortium.
overlap: No overlap with the active non-culprit lesion NMA in STEMI (different population and comparison).
target_journal: Circulation or JACC (European Heart Journal as alternative)

G1.note: PCI for stable coronary disease is among the most common procedures; the decision concerns death and MI.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); G2 judged on trial evidence only. The two pooled analyses disagree on cardiac death (RR 0.79, 0.67-0.93 versus all-cause RR 0.99, 0.90-1.09 in different outcome sets, PMIDs 34002203 and 32794407).

G3.note: No adequately powered RCT of the whole comparison reports within 24 months; ongoing trials cover CTO (NCT03563417, 2028-11) or ischaemic cardiomyopathy (NCT07349979, 2028-01; NCT05828719, 2028-07). Latest meta-analyses in the subset are from 2020 and 2021; trials published since include REVIVED (700 patients, PMID 36027563). A search outside the appraised subset for a 2024 to 2026 target-journal meta-analysis is still required.

G4.note: Reconstructed-IPD time-varying analysis addresses non-proportional hazards, which fixed relative risks cannot; a guideline committee would cite it. A conventional meta-analysis would repeat the existing disagreement.

G5.note: Not a repeat of the same trials: adds post-2021 trials and a different estimand. Risk that the added sample is modest; the adversarial check should quantify the added patients.

impact.why: Stable coronary disease PCI and CABG decisions are very frequent and concern hard outcomes.

novelty.why: Meta-analyses exist, but time-varying effects by presentation have not been shown in the appraised subset.

equipoise.why: Pooled analyses and individual trials disagree on cardiac death and spontaneous MI.

design.why: Reconstructed IPD is credible for time-to-event outcomes but limited by MI definition heterogeneity and the lack of covariates.

timeliness.why: Recent long-term follow-ups (PMIDs 36335918, 41540107) change the evidence, but no single readout forces the timing.

citation.why: Comparable synthesis papers appear in Circulation and EHJ (PMIDs 32794407, 34002203); the benchmark has not yet been run.

feasibility.why: Matches the owner's reconstructed-IPD and network meta-analysis skills.

Extract Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk from PMIDs 32227755, 36335918, 41540107, 36027563 and the trials in PMIDs 32794407 and 34002203.
